clue.text: Flyer's half-playful title

definitions.note: a possessive in the clue, but the definition is the noun: an aircraft maker's plane

indicators.note: half of the play's doubled title is wanted, so only its first part of the two identical words is kept

parts.note: a play's title: the farce ...-..., a stage comedy about airline hostesses

explanation.surface: A pilot's half-jokey nickname or rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playful' here means 'of a play': the farce Boeing-Boeing repeats its word, so half the title is one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boeing company's airliners are the best-known aircraft in the sky, so the name stands for a plane.

clue.text: So Madam hasn't changed !

parts.note: read the word Madam from right to left and it stays the same: it is a palindrome

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a lady has not changed at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelled in reverse, from last letter to first, a palindrome like Madam reads identically.

clue.text: Getting level by the end of the day?

explanation.surface: A question about catching up with rivals before nightfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening a score is making it equal; evening is also the late part of the day, around dusk.

clue.text: P.M's rage with Austen at the Abbey

parts.note: Lord North was British Prime Minister during the American Revolution
anger means rage

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister fumes over Jane Austen visiting an abbey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is a link word. Northanger Abbey is Austen's Gothic parody novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's novel Northanger Abbey is named for the house in it, the abbey of her title.

clue.text: No charge for air-drop

parts.note: read one way, a parachute jump that costs nothing; read the other, a drop through the air before the canopy opens, with nothing holding the jumper

explanation.surface: An airline or skydiving club advertises jumps at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A skydiver's unchecked plunge before the parachute opens is literally a fall with nothing to pay or to restrain it.

clue.text: They show the effects of second sight

definitions.text: They show the effects of second sight

parts.words: They show the effects of second sight
parts.note: second sight sounds psychic, but here it is a second look at a text, leading to changes

explanation.surface: A remark about clairvoyants' visions.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors' amendments come from going over a draft again, a second look.

clue.text: Return the dress to York

indicators.note: return means the garment word is turned round and read the other way

parts.note: a robe is a dress or gown

explanation.surface: Instructions to send a garment back to a shop in York.
explanation.walkthrough: EBOR is short for Eboracum, the Roman name of York, used in the Archbishop of York's signature and the Ebor horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebor is the Latin-derived name for the city, from its Roman name Eboracum.

clue.text: Florentine New World name

parts.note: the explorer from Florence whose first name was given to the Americas

explanation.surface: A Tuscan name for something new.
explanation.definitionFit: Amerigo Vespucci, a navigator from Florence, gave his Latinised first name to the continents of America.

clue.text: Turner in Scala Theatre ?

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: The painter J.M.W. Turner appears at a theatre called the Scala.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter but means a machine that turns wood or metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe spins a workpiece so it can be shaped, making it a machine that turns things.

clue.text: The Lido image

parts.note: the letters of Lido rearranged give a word for an image or false god

explanation.surface: A picture of the Venice beach called the Lido.
explanation.definitionFit: A worshipped statue, a graven image, is an object of idolatry.

clue.text: Alexandria quartet girl a Communist ? Acquitted

parts.note: Clea is the title heroine of the last novel in Lawrence Durrell's Alexandria Quartet
red is the usual crossword word for a communist

explanation.surface: A question about whether a heroine of Durrell's novels was a Communist, ending with her acquittal.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' between the pieces is a link word only. Durrell's Alexandria Quartet is four novels: Justine, Balthazar, Mountolive and Clea.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant who is acquitted has had their name cleared by the court.

clue.text: Intense colour with no initial ingredient

indicators.note: an ingredient goes into a mix, so the letter becomes part of the colour word

parts.note: violet is a colour of the spectrum

indicators.note: the initial of the word 'no' is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dye described as strong in colour but lacking its first component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no initial ingredient' looks like something missing; in fact the N of 'no' is added into VIOLET.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent feelings or storms are extreme in force, the same sense as intense.

clue.text: Not so much delay we hear in space ?

indicators.note: the phrase says the words before it are to be heard as they sound, not as they are spelt

parts.note: less wait, said as 'wait-less'

explanation.surface: Someone notes there is less waiting in outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts in orbit float free, experiencing no gravity, which is the state the definition describes.

clue.text: Stake your fortune

explanation.surface: A gambler is told to bet everything they own.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake is a post driven into the ground, as a pile is in building; and to make one's pile is to make a fortune.

clue.text: Magniloquent heraldic epithet

explanation.surface: A description of grand speech in heraldry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heraldic' means of a herald: Stentor was the loud-voiced herald of the Greeks in Homer's Iliad.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentorian means very loud and booming in voice, and the word comes from the name of a Homeric herald.

clue.text: Style only suitable for the minority as a rule

definitions.text: only suitable for the minority as a rule

explanation.surface: A fashion said to suit only a few people, generally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minority' means a monarch being under age, not a small group; 'rule' means government, not 'as a rule' = usually.
explanation.definitionFit: The early-1800s English furniture and architecture style takes its name from the period when the Prince of Wales governed for his incapable father, as is done for an infant monarch.

clue.text: Jaundiced youth as sovereign

parts.note: jaundice turns the skin yellow
a boy is a youth

explanation.surface: A sickly young man ascends the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is a link word. 'Sovereign' is the gold coin, not a monarch; yellowboy was slang for a gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellowboy is old slang for a gold coin, and a sovereign is a British gold coin worth a pound.

clue.text: Defeat high-handedly

parts.note: high-handed literally: beating someone with a show of raised hands in a ballot

explanation.surface: Beating an opponent arrogantly.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion is beaten in a vote when more hands go up against it than for it.

clue.text: But they still carry weight economically

definitions.text: But they still carry weight economically

parts.words: But they still carry weight economically
parts.note: former porters who, though no longer carrying luggage, still matter in trade

explanation.surface: A comment that some people remain influential in economics.
explanation.definitionFit: Firms selling goods abroad are important to a country's trade balance, so they carry weight.

clue.text: Fish sketched by Landseer ? Not right, somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the remaining letters are put together in some other way
not means the letter for the word after it is left out of the painter's name

explanation.surface: A fish drawn by the Victorian animal painter Landseer, judged badly done.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R from LANDSEER, leaving LANDSEE, and rearrange those letters. Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The sand eel is a small slender sea fish that burrows into sand.

clue.text: Power can rule by reaction

indicators.note: in a reaction elements recombine, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A government is said to rule through a reactionary response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reaction' suggests politics, and also hints at the chain reaction in a reactor.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear power is electricity from atomic reactors, so the word stands for a kind of power.

clue.text: Anyone caught here gets a tanning

definitions.text: Anyone caught here gets a tanning

parts.words: Anyone caught here gets a tanning
parts.note: a tanning sounds like a beating for someone caught, but here it is a suntan in a sheltered sunny spot

explanation.surface: A warning that intruders caught on the premises will be thrashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltered spot that catches and holds the sun's warmth, where people sunbathe.

clue.text: What to do before you retire ?

definitions.text: What to do before you retire

parts.words: What to do before you retire
parts.note: retire read as re-tyre: before fitting new tyres you may put a new tread on old ones

explanation.surface: Advice to someone about to stop working or go to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a fresh rubber surface on a worn tyre saves buying a new one.

clue.text: It's hard to manage one course after another

definitions.text: It's hard to manage one course after another

parts.words: It's hard to manage one course after another
parts.note: a sailing boat zigzags against the wind, on one heading then another; also hard ship's biscuit served course after course

explanation.surface: A diner complains about getting through a long meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' is a heading for a sailing boat, not a dish; hard tack was also the ship's biscuit sailors ate.
explanation.definitionFit: To sail into the wind a boat changes heading back and forth, each leg being one such move.

clue.text: Overflows the sides so to speak?

indicators.note: so to speak says the word for the sides is to be heard spoken, not written

parts.note: the sides in a match are teams

explanation.surface: A river spills over its banks, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: A place that teems with something is crowded with it, as if full to bursting.

clue.text: Resting-place for second class mail ?

parts.note: a bed, read as somewhere 'for poster', a place for mailing done after first class

explanation.surface: Where slower post sits waiting to be delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand bed with a tall post at each corner, the resting-place of the definition.

clue.text: Pity the gleaner

explanation.surface: Feeling sorry for a farm worker picking up leftover grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is an old word for compassion (as in ruthless); and the biblical Ruth gleaned in the fields of Boaz.

clue.text: That's the point of the 'wire, old horse !

explanation.surface: Someone explains the purpose of a fence to an old horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The barb is the spike on barbed wire; a barb is also a horse of the Barbary breed from North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The sharp spike is what makes the fence wire hurt; the Barbary breed of horse was prized in older times.

clue.text: She was all the poor chap had

definitions.text: She was all the poor chap had

parts.words: She was all the poor chap had
parts.note: the prophet Nathan's parable in 2 Samuel 12, where the poor man has nothing but one little female lamb

explanation.surface: A remark about a poor man's only companion or wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' suggests a wife; the Bible story's poor man owned only one young female sheep, taken by a rich neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A young female sheep, the single possession of the poor man in Nathan's parable to King David.

clue.text: Old naval unit of III Corps

parts.note: Roman three, giving the prefix tri-
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A naval unit belonging to an army corps numbered three.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Greek or Roman warship with three banks of oars was a unit of an old fleet.

clue.text: Back American gunners to bracket a bay in Java

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for the American nation is read the other way

parts.note: US, the United States, stands for American

indicators.note: to bracket something is to stand on either side of it, so the other letters enclose the word bay

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners

explanation.surface: Instructions for soldiers to support American artillery straddling a bay in Java.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bracket' means stand either side of, not support. 'Back' turns only the American abbreviation. The definition 'in Java' is loose: it names a place found on that island.
explanation.definitionFit: Surabaya is a major port city on the island of Java, Indonesia.

clue.text: Poles are so positive

parts.note: Poles look like people from Poland being confident; here they are electrical terminals carrying positive charge

explanation.surface: A claim that Polish people are always sure of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The positive electrodes of a battery or cell are its plus poles.
